title: The Vampire at Table Seven
excerpt: He visits the same café every evening, orders coffee he never drinks, and watches the door.

sections.title: Table Seven
paragraphs: Every evening at 6:40, the pale man took table seven and ordered a black coffee.
Every evening at 7:15, the coffee was still untouched.
June noticed because noticing customers was part of her job. She noticed everything else because she was curious.

sections.title: The Question
paragraphs: On the twenty-first evening, she asked him why he came.
He looked toward the door and said, 'I promised someone I would wait.'
'How long?' she asked. He smiled without humor. 'Since 1891.'

sections.title: Closing Time
paragraphs: The person he had waited for never came.
But when June switched off the café lights, he stood for the first time before closing.
Sometimes eternity ends not when the past returns, but when something in the present finally asks you to leave with it.
